newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: South Africa money mkt shortage jumps to 9.81 bln rand.
newsitem.headline: South Africa money mkt shortage jumps to 9.81 bln rand.

text.p: South Africa's daily money market shortage for Tuesday jumped to 9.810 billion rand from Monday's 9.110 billion rand, the Reserve Bank said.
The high shortage, reflecting a liquidity squeeze in the wake of the latest sell-off in the rand and South African assets, has fuelled fears of a hike in interest rates.
Short-term rates, which were marked up sharply at the start of the week, are already more than discounting a one percentage point increase in the key Bank rate, currently 16 percent.
On Wednesday, commercial banks held their three-month NCD rates steady at between 16.85 and 17.10 percent, while the 90-day BA rate was unchanged at 16.25 to 16.45 percent.
Money market traders said pressure on liquidity would continue until around the end of January as Christmas spending was likely to exacerbate the situation.
